meta.title: OpenPlanner – video appointments that land in your contact center
meta.description: Open-source scheduling for video appointments on Webex. People book a time on a page in your house style and join from the browser; the call arrives in Webex Contact Center for the first free agent. Personal data is deleted 24 hours after the call.

hero.eyebrow: Open source · for Webex Contact Center · WCAG 2.2 AA
hero.lead: People book a video call with your team on a page in your house style, and join from their browser: no app, no account. Five minutes before the start, the call arrives in Webex Contact Center like any other contact, and the first free agent picks it up. A day after the call, the personal data is deleted.

facts.label: apps or accounts the person you call needs
before the start, the call is in your agents' queue
after the call, the personal data is deleted

hero.command:
git clone https://github.com/3Corners-Labs/OpenPlanner && cd OpenPlanner
cp .env.example .env
docker compose --profile dev up --build -d
docker compose exec web python -m app.cli seed-demo
hero.command_label: For developers: run it on a laptop in five minutes, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/g/demo

tour.title: From booking to conversation
tour.lead: Follow both sides: what the person you serve sees, from picking a time to the call, and what your team sees, from planning the staffing to picking up.

steps.title: Picking a time
steps.text: A month calendar, the free times of a day and a short form: name, email and, if you want, a few questions of your own. On your own web address, in your house style.

steps.title: Or talk right away
steps.text: When the team is open, people can start a call on the spot. You decide how many may wait, and they see honestly how long it will take.

steps.title: Confirmed by email
steps.text: One click confirms the booking. Then a calendar invite, a personal link and a reminder before the start. By text message too, if you want.

steps.title: Move or cancel
steps.text: Through the personal link, no account needed. Cancel up to the start, move up to an hour before; what they filled in is already there.

steps.title: Test the video first
steps.text: A short trial call on Webex checks camera, microphone and sound before it matters. Your team sees in the agenda who has tested.

steps.title: Joining the call
steps.text: One click in the browser, no app or account. Each appointment is its own Webex meeting; they wait in the lobby until the agent joins.

steps.title: Several organisations, one installation
steps.text: Each organisation has its own teams, house style, texts, channels and sign-in. Roles come from your own sign-in system: administrator, planner, agent, auditor.

steps.title: Teams work like skills
steps.text: Each team has its own queue, opening hours, form and texts. People never pick a person; the call goes to the first free agent.

steps.title: Staffing per block
steps.text: Say how many agents are on duty in each block of the day, with holidays and exceptions. Only times you can staff are offered. Need to close at short notice? One action, and people are asked to pick a new time.

steps.title: Agenda and planner, live
steps.text: Every appointment and its state: booked, video tested, in the call, finished. Planners move or cancel on someone's behalf and see why something failed.

steps.title: In the queue five minutes before
steps.text: Five minutes before the start, the call arrives as a work item in Webex Contact Center, or in OpenPlanner's own queue for a team without a contact center. You choose per team.

steps.title: The agent picks up
steps.text: The agent takes the call from the queue, sees only a first name, and joins the meeting as cohost. A day after the call, the personal data is deleted.

how.title: Up and running in three steps

steps.title: Set up a team
steps.text: In the portal a team is called a group: opening hours, staffing, holidays, texts and house style, all in one place. No code, no developer needed.

steps.title: Link to its booking page
steps.text: Each team gets its own booking page on your web address. Link to it from your website, or place the calendar right inside one of your pages.

steps.title: Calls arrive by themselves
steps.text: In Webex Contact Center as a work item, or in OpenPlanner's own queue where agents pick them up. You choose per team.

features.title: Everything a video appointment needs, nothing more
features.lead: Made for teams that help many people by video: customer service, advice desks, intake and support.

items.title: Booking without hurdles
items.text: A calendar, the free times and a short form. People confirm by email and move or cancel through a personal link. Works without JavaScript and fully by keyboard.

items.title: Webex built in
items.text: Every appointment gets its own Webex meeting. Your visitor joins from the browser, with no app or account; your agent joins as cohost.

items.title: Lands where your agents work
items.text: The call arrives in the Webex Contact Center queue as a work item, or in OpenPlanner's own queue for teams without a contact center. The first free agent picks up; nobody has to watch a calendar.

items.title: Talk right away
items.text: When a team is open, it can offer a call on the spot, with a limit on how many people wait and an honest waiting time.

items.title: Many organisations, clear roles
items.text: One installation serves several organisations, each with its own teams, house style, texts and sign-in. One rights model decides who sees and does what.

items.title: Teams, not individuals
items.text: Each team works like a skill in your contact center, with its own queue and opening hours. Visitors never choose a person; the first free agent picks up.

items.title: Privacy by design
items.text: Personal data is kept only with the appointment and deleted 24 hours after the call. Never in logs, web addresses or error messages.

items.title: Your house style, your words
items.text: Colours, logo and font per organisation, and every text editable in the portal. Dutch and English included, more languages possible.

items.title: Messages that arrive
items.text: Confirmation, change, reminder and cancellation by email with a calendar invite, and by text message. The portal checks that your mail domain is set up to be trusted (SPF, DKIM, DMARC).

items.title: Planning and agenda
items.text: Follow every call live, plan staffing per block, and close a team in one action when you must; people then pick a new time themselves.

integrations.title: Built around Webex, open to the rest
integrations.lead: OpenPlanner is not a video platform and not a contact center. It connects the Webex products you already have, and keeps every other system behind its own connector, so each one can be replaced.

items.name: Webex Meetings
items.text: Every appointment is a real Webex meeting. People join straight from the browser, can do a trial call first, and your agenda shows live who is in the call.

items.name: Webex Contact Center
items.text: Five minutes before the start, the call becomes a work item in your team's queue, carrying only the reference, a first name, the team and the join link. No contact center? A team can use OpenPlanner's own queue.

items.name: Webex Messaging
items.text: Planned: a bot tells administrators in Webex when the integration falters, a queue fills up or a check fails. Never personal data, always a link to the portal.

items.name: Your identity provider
items.text: Administrators sign in with the identity provider that comes with OpenPlanner, managed in the portal, or with your own (PingFederate, Entra ID, Keycloak or any OpenID Connect provider), chosen per organisation by email domain. A second factor can be required.

items.name: Email and SMS
items.text: Email through your own mail server and text messages through an SMS gateway, per organisation. Every text editable per channel and per team.

items.name: AI agents and bots
items.text: A contact-center bot, such as the Webex AI Agent, can look up free times and book on someone's behalf, through an API with its own keys and permissions.

integrations.roadmap: Other contact-center platforms on the same connectors, health checks with a fallback per team, subjects and routing per team, bots that can change bookings, and staff provisioned from your directory.

enterprise.title: Ready for IT, security and procurement
enterprise.lead: Your IT and security colleagues will ask how it is built, where the data goes and who can change what. Here are the answers, and they are checked automatically on every change, not just promised.

plate.title: What runs where
plate.lead: One server you manage yourself, with two containers and one database. Everything else is a system you already have, connected through its own connector.

people.name: Participant
people.sub: browser or widget, no account, no app

people.name: Administrators and planners
people.sub: admin portal, sign-in at your own IdP

people.name: Agents
people.sub: work item in Webex Contact Center or OpenPlanner's own queue

people.name: Bots
people.sub: machine API with OAuth client credentials

host.name: HTTPS proxy
host.sub: Caddy: Let's Encrypt or your own certificate

host.name: worker
host.sub: scheduled jobs: meetings, messages, work items, deleting personal data

host.name: SQLite (WAL)
host.sub: personal data only with the appointment, deleted 24 hours after the call

host.name: host updater
host.sub: checks the signature, takes a backup, rolls back on its own

plate.host_note: Containers run without root on a read-only filesystem.

systems.name: Webex Contact Center
systems.sub: work item with a first name and the join link

systems.name: Email and SMS
systems.sub: SMTP and SMS gateway, per organisation

systems.name: Webex Messaging
systems.sub: alerts to administrators, without personal data

flows: The participant books over HTTPS; the data stays in the database on your server.
The worker creates the Webex meeting and sends the confirmation and reminders by email or SMS.
Five minutes before the start, the contact center gets a work item with only the reference, the first name, the team and the join link.
Administrators sign in at your own identity provider; every decision goes to the audit log, which you can ship to your own log systems.
Updates arrive as signed images; the host updater checks the signature before it switches.
plate.caption: Simplified. The full plate, with every flow and the decision behind it, is in the repository.

enterprise.arch_caption: Each layer depends only on the layer below it. An automatic check on every change refuses code that breaks this.

layers.name: Domain
layers.note: Pure Python, no framework, ≥ 90% test coverage

pillars.title: One core, replaceable edges
pillars.text: Another contact center or video platform means a new connector. Your teams, screens and texts stay as they are.

pillars.title: Checked, not promised
pillars.text: Structure, types, rights and privacy rules are checked automatically on every change. What fails never ships.

pillars.title: One source for each subject
pillars.text: Rights, settings and the portal's structure each live in one place, and their documentation is generated from the code, so it cannot drift.

pillars.title: Decision by decision on record
pillars.text: Every design decision is in the repository with its context, its choice, its settings and what has been built of it. An architect reads why things are the way they are, and what does not run yet.

scale.title: Today: one server, with room to spare
scale.text: Proxy, web and worker on one virtual machine with SQLite. One installation serves many organisations; growing means more processor power, memory and a faster disk.

scale.title: A known limit
scale.text: Designed for around 80 appointments per working day. The scaling plan says when we move on: above 2,000 appointments a working day, when responses slow past one second, when stricter availability is required, or when a client requires managed Postgres.

scale.title: After that: designed, not yet built
scale.text: Postgres, several web servers behind the proxy and workers on more machines. All database access already goes through one connector, so teams, screens and texts stay the same.

scale_link.label: Scaling envelope and the path beyond one VM

items.title: One rights model
items.text: Who may do what is defined in one table of roles, rights and levels. Every screen and action checks it, and every refusal is logged. No exceptions, not even for the superuser.

items.title: Organisations kept apart
items.text: An organisation administrator never sees another organisation, a team administrator never another team. The menu, the buttons and the API follow the same rules.

items.title: Single sign-on, nothing on the side
items.text: OIDC with PKCE, state and nonce, asymmetric algorithms only, sessions held on the server, a second factor that can be required. No local accounts, no break-glass login, on purpose.

items.title: An audit trail you can forward
items.text: Sign-ins, changes and refusals as structured events, sent to syslog, Splunk or Elastic if you want. Without personal data.

items.title: Signed releases
items.text: Images signed keyless with cosign, an SBOM (CycloneDX) on every release, CVE scans with trivy and grype, hashes in the lockfile. The installation verifies the signature.

items.title: A strict pipeline
items.text: Type checks, security scanners, secret scanning, mutation tests, API fuzzing, OWASP ZAP and accessibility tests with axe-core and Lighthouse. Any failure blocks the change.

items.title: Light to run
items.text: Two containers and one database file. HTTPS with automatic certificates or your own proxy, updates from the portal, and the backup is one file.

items.title: Accessible, provably
items.text: WCAG 2.2 AA on every public page, in every language, tested again on every pull request. No time limits, no CAPTCHA puzzles.

items.title: Configurable, not hard-coded
items.text: Every threshold, limit and period is a setting with a class, a default and bounds. What is a protection cannot be switched off from the portal.

opensource.title: Open source, open decisions
opensource.lead: OpenPlanner is published under the EUPL-1.2, the open-source licence of the European Commission. Not only the code is open: every design decision sits in the repository, with what has been built of it.

points.title: EUPL-1.2
points.text: Use, change and distribute it, commercially too. Compatible with GPL, AGPL and most European procurement rules.

points.title: Decisions on record
points.text: Every design decision has its context, choice, settings and build status in the repository. You read why things are the way they are, and what does not run yet.

points.title: Security up front
points.text: A threat model per flow, an abuse case per endpoint, each with a test. Responsible disclosure through SECURITY.md.

points.title: Contributions welcome
points.text: Issues, discussions and pull requests on GitHub. A CLA keeps the licence clean. Every PR answers the same seven review questions.

releases.title: Releases
releases.lead: Every merged change becomes a release candidate for test environments; stable releases follow from those. Each one is a signed image with a software bill of materials (SBOM). This website is updated with every minor or major release.
releases.none: No release on this channel yet.

releases.fresh: When this page loads, your browser asks GitHub for the current release list and for nothing else: no cookie, no account, no storage. The list built into the page is what you see when GitHub does not answer.

standards.title: Standards, with the evidence
standards.lead: Every claim below points to the code, a test or the pipeline, with an honest status: done, partly done or planned.
code: Python 3.12 with full type checking (mypy strict) and ruff for style and common mistakes.
A layered architecture, enforced with import-linter: the domain knows no framework.
Every module and function with a Google-style docstring, readable by documentation tools.
Test coverage ≥ 90% on the domain and translations, mutation score ≥ 80%, abuse cases as tests.
Conventional Commits, one recorded decision per choice with its build status, and every PR answers seven review questions.
bandit, semgrep, gitleaks, pip-audit and a licence check on every pull request.
update: The superuser picks the channel in the portal: stable, or release candidate for a test environment.
Install a new version with one click in the portal, or let the installation do it by itself.
The host verifies the signature of every image before the update; an unsigned image does not run.
Renovate keeps dependencies current weekly, security updates at once; a PR older than 14 days raises an alert.
Database migrations run automatically and can always be rolled back.

items.name: WCAG 2.2 AA (EN 301 549)
items.what: Keyboard flow, axe-core with zero violations and Lighthouse ≥ 95 on every public page, in every language, on every pull request. Manual audit with NVDA and VoiceOver before go-live.

items.name: NL Design System
items.what: Colours, type and spacing of the participant pages come from NL Design System tokens; organisations adjust them within those tokens.

items.name: HTTPS, HSTS and NCSC TLS guidelines
items.what: HTTPS with HSTS (Forum Standaardisatie comply-or-explain list), TLS 1.2 and 1.3 per the NCSC guidelines. A script checks the TLS versions, HSTS and the round trip of the public address; internet.nl is in the go-live checklist.

items.name: SPF, DKIM and DMARC
items.what: Comply-or-explain standards for email. The portal checks each organisation's sender domain and shows what is missing.

items.name: OpenID Connect
items.what: Administrators sign in through their own identity provider: PKCE, state and nonce, asymmetric algorithms only. Tested against Keycloak, built for PingFederate at the first client.

items.name: OpenAPI 3
items.what: The API specification is generated from the code, compared on every pull request and attacked with schemathesis.

items.name: GDPR and privacy by design
items.what: Personal data only with the appointment, deleted 24 hours after the call, never in logs. The data-flow diagram is the input for the organisation's DPIA.

items.name: Building blocks for the BIO
items.what: An audit log of every change and denial, security events on attacks, an auditor role and export to your log platform. The BIO itself remains the organisation's responsibility.

items.name: security.txt (RFC 9116)
items.what: A fixed reporting point for vulnerabilities on every installation, with SECURITY.md in the repository.

items.name: Software supply chain
items.what: Every image signed keyless with cosign, a CycloneDX SBOM with every release, CVE scans with trivy and grype, dependencies pinned with hashes.

items.name: Standard for Public Code
items.what: EUPL-1.2, a licence per file through REUSE, decisions public in the repository, and a publiccode.yml that CI validates and every release updates. The listing on developer.overheid.nl is still open.

items.name: Penetration test
items.what: An external penetration test before go-live and yearly after. Until then: OWASP ZAP on every merge and abuse cases as tests.

roadmap.title: What comes next
roadmap.lead: Decided and not built yet. Everything above this section runs today; the open work is public on GitHub.

items.title: Other contact centers
items.text: The same hand-over to platforms other than Webex Contact Center, behind the adapter that already exists.

items.title: Health checks and fallback
items.text: The connection to the contact center is checked all the time; administrators get an alert by email or in a Webex space, and a team can fall back to OpenPlanner's own queue when the contact center is down.

items.title: Subjects and routing
items.text: A subject and routing attributes per team from a fixed list, so the contact center sends the call to the right skill.

items.title: Rebooking assistant
items.text: When a team falls short, the participant is offered a new time and keeps the place until they answer.

items.title: Bots can change bookings
items.text: A contact-center bot that today offers free times and books can also move and cancel on the participant's behalf.

items.title: Staff through SCIM
items.text: Staff and roles provisioned from your directory, without typing them in the portal.

items.title: Configuration as a document
items.text: Compare and apply a whole configuration as one JSON document, with a plan of what will change first.

involved.title: Start today, or help build it
involved.lead: OpenPlanner is built in the open by a small team. Look around, put it on a server, or take a piece of the work: you are welcome at every step.

paths.title: Try it
paths.text: Book a call on the demo page above, or have your IT team run the full demo on a laptop in five minutes: a demo team, a mailbox that catches every email, and a test user for every role.

paths.title: Run it
paths.text: One install script gives a test or production server HTTPS, signed images and automatic updates. Start with a release candidate and tell us what you find.

paths.title: Help build it
paths.text: Developers pick a good first issue. Testers try a release candidate or walk the booking page with a screen reader. Translators add a language. Security researchers report responsibly.
